nodes.rationale: The one notification authorization surface { state: unknown | not_determined | granted | denied, observed_at } introduced here and consumed by P4; unknown is not-yet-observed while not_determined is an observed outcome, and no Info.plist usage-description string or entitlement is required for local notifications.

nodes.label: Set-up-again recovery from shared service (D-H9)
nodes.rationale: On a start on the same account with connectivity, recovery resolves the household from the shared service which is the source of truth, with no empty-household or onboarding state and no import, migration or local backup.

nodes.label: SharingPolicy configuration values
nodes.rationale: Per-device configuration (15 s attempt bound, 5 s reachability-probe bound, 3-consecutive-failure offline threshold) consumed from P0's design rather than re-derived, kept out of the household collection.

nodes.label: Visible household-naming notification (D-H14)
nodes.rationale: A change delivered while the product is not open is visible and raises a local notification naming the household only, carrying no health content (no rabbit name, symptom, note, weight or medication name), because a lock-screen notification would otherwise publish the household's health content.

nodes.label: Load once per data area (D6.3)
nodes.rationale: Each data area is loaded once and reused, keyed by household and data area so switching the active household cannot serve one household's cached area for another; opening a partially loaded rabbit requests only what is missing.

nodes.label: Scoped invalidation by per-item version (D6.4)
nodes.rationale: A remote change reuses the existing household:changed event with kind: refreshed and compares per-item version/updated_at so only affected query keys are invalidated; an unscoped refresh-everything signal would recreate the historical full reload on the next visit.

nodes.label: Two cache layers, two jobs
nodes.rationale: The local copy in the product's own storage decides whether a read contacts the shared service and whether the freshness window elapsed, while the in-memory frontend query cache decides whether navigation re-invokes a read; conflating the two is how the optimisation goes wrong, and the frontend cache is derived with the local copy as the only cache of record.

nodes.label: Why P6 lands last
nodes.rationale: P0 deliberately left the loaded-data path unoptimised (D0.2), fixing only the boundaries, so this change can improve read behaviour without moving them; it is only meaningful once the phases that populate the read path exist.

nodes.label: NFR-7 Bounded cold load and load-once reuse
nodes.norm_label: nfr-7 bounded cold load and load-once reuse

nodes.label: CI-asserted count vs recorded wall-clock (D6.7)
nodes.rationale: The request count is a requirement asserted in CI because it is deterministic and environment-independent, while the wall-clock figure is recorded measurement evidence taken once on the reference device and never a pass/fail CI assertion, so the gate does not become a simulator-timing lottery.

nodes.label: Fixed two-request cold load bound (D6.1)
nodes.rationale: A cold dashboard load is one fixed set of parallel requests covering the dashboard's areas: the household collection plus one account/service-status check, independent of rabbit count; the value is settled as two and owned by this change, sitting alongside P0's D0.13 constants rather than re-derived, and exceeding two fails the bound even if the load is fast.

nodes.label: 30-second global freshness window (D6.2)
nodes.rationale: Already-loaded data is served first and a load inside its freshness window does not contact the shared service; the window is one named configurable global value of 30 seconds so tests can drive it to zero, and a change signal is honoured regardless of it while freshness is never claimed.

nodes.label: Optimisation behind the existing contract (D6.5)
nodes.rationale: This change adds no command, event, type or capability; the read path improves behind load_household and the surrounding read commands, deliberately avoiding a preload-everything command because an explicit bulk endpoint would be a contract change in service of an implementation detail.

nodes.label: Offline member deletion window (D-H15)
nodes.rationale: A member whose device is offline at deletion keeps reading previously loaded data until the device next reaches the shared service, when the cached copy is dropped and access is gone; no remote-wipe mechanism is promised because deleting an unreachable device's copy is impossible.

nodes.label: Owner-gated irreversible deletion cascade (D-H5)
nodes.rationale: Ownership gates exactly one operation, household deletion, enforced at the storage boundary not the UI; deletion removes the household and all its data in one irreversible step with no undo or restore, and the newest remaining household becomes active or onboarding is presented.

nodes.label: Archive order P0-P1-P2-P3-P5-P4-P6
nodes.rationale: Every change after P0 modifies capability specs P0 opened, so archives must run strictly in order; P5 archives before P4 because export and medication reminders read P5's medication model, and P6 stays last.

nodes.label: HS-10 Only the owner can permanently delete a household

nodes.label: Active/finished derived from end date (D5.2)
nodes.rationale: Status is computed on read from the end date and the present moment and never persisted, so setting the end date to today finishes the course immediately by construction and a stored status cannot disagree with its date or put a background job in the read path.

nodes.label: Derived affordance set for read-only states (D5.6)
nodes.norm_label: derived affordance set for read-only states (d5.6)
nodes.rationale: Because the two exceptions a finished medication permits are narrower than a single read-only flag can express, the contract carries a derived affordance set computed on read and never stored, mirrored in the UI and enforced at the write boundary; hiding a control is not enforcement.

nodes.label: Enumerated units with no conversion (D5.7)
nodes.rationale: The serving unit is exactly {mg, ml, drops, tablets} with no canonical unit and no conversion anywhere, because inventing mg-to-ml for a drug would be a clinical claim; a dose carries its own value and unit which may differ from the serving's.

nodes.label: Dose giver captured from recording member (D5.4, DM-5)
nodes.norm_label: dose giver captured from recording member (d5.4, dm-5)
nodes.rationale: A dose's giver is the authenticated member who recorded it, stored as the member id and resolved at read time through P0's fallback chain; there is no giver picker and the giver is not among MED-6's editable attributes, so attribution is non-retargetable by construction.

nodes.label: Informational active-medication badge (D5.8)
nodes.rationale: DASH-5's badge says a rabbit is on something, which is information not alarm, so it is rendered in informational styling visually distinct from the warning flag and never adopts warning styling; it is a pure derivation from the derived medication status and is presented without a hover.

nodes.label: Neutral schedule value type, four variants (D5.3)
nodes.norm_label: neutral schedule value type, four variants (d5.3)

nodes.label: Invitation acceptance as household adoption (D-H3)
nodes.rationale: Acceptance records an adoption-in-progress before any household exists locally so the route guard never falls back to creation onboarding while data is arriving; a household created during the wait wins and stays active, and a non-completed acceptance writes a redacted diagnostic record.

nodes.label: Member cap enforced at membership level (D-H13)
nodes.norm_label: member cap enforced at membership level (d-h13)
nodes.rationale: The six-member cap is a property of the household's membership, so an invitation is refused when the household already holds six and accepting an outstanding invitation into a full household is refused with the same six-member-limit explanation; enforcing only at invitation creation would let an issued invitation carry the household past six.

nodes.label: One invitation per household, resolved by reuse (D-H2)
nodes.norm_label: one invitation per household, resolved by reuse (d-h2)
nodes.rationale: A household holds at most one invitation; creation verifies availability, reuses an existing invitation instead of creating a second, and otherwise creates one, making re-inviting idempotent in the user-visible sense that killed the historical already-shared failure.

nodes.label: Client-generated request_id idempotency
nodes.rationale: Every state-changing command carries a client-generated request_id the shared service deduplicates on, so a retry re-invokes the same command and is idempotent by construction rather than producing a second invitation or second deletion.

nodes.label: Convergence as primary risk (R1)
nodes.rationale: P3's subject is not new feature surface but convergence: two identities, one household, one set of data, and a user-visible outcome for every path that can fail; every requirement is written so it can be tested by taking two accounts through the same household.

nodes.label: Near-simultaneous dose guard (D5.5, MED-7)
nodes.rationale: The guard is a read-then-confirm rule presenting a warning the person can continue past or cancel, deliberately not a stored lock, uniqueness constraint or persisted flag; the check performs no write so cancelling leaves the collection untouched and it is safe to repeat.

nodes.label: Medication registry, dosing record and double-dosing guard
nodes.norm_label: medication registry, dosing record and double-dosing guard

nodes.label: Single bounded-time sharing attempt (D-H1)
nodes.rationale: Invitation creation and acceptance are each a single attempt with a deadline resolving as success or a SaveCause.timeout failure; nothing is queued or retried in the background, so there is no ambiguous half-accepted state (D1 applied to sharing), accepting the consequence that a person cannot invite or accept while the service is unreachable.

nodes.label: Guard window anchored on entered timestamp (D5.12)
nodes.norm_label: guard window anchored on entered timestamp (d5.12)
nodes.rationale: The approximately 15-minute window is measured from the timestamp entered for the new dose and covers doses both before and after it; anchoring on confirmation breaks back-dating a forgotten dose and a backward-only reading misses a back-dated dose colliding with a later one.

nodes.label: Fresh read of medication doses at confirm (D5.13)
nodes.norm_label: fresh read of medication doses at confirm (d5.13)
nodes.rationale: Confirming a dose re-reads that medication's doses from the shared collection before the window is evaluated rather than trusting the device copy, because the dose the guard exists to catch is precisely one a stale copy will not hold; this resolves R1 at the cost of a slower confirmation on a path that already requires a reachable service.

nodes.label: Medication writes stay connectivity-required (D5.1)
nodes.rationale: Every medication and dose write goes through P0's reachability gate with no local write queue, no optimistic write and no pending-dose state, accepting that US-MED-23 offline dose logging stays dropped and that a dose another member recorded moments ago may not yet be present locally.

nodes.label: Component Tokens Layer

nodes.label: Primitive Tokens
nodes.rationale: Raw values carry no meaning so they change rarely; semantic naming is deferred to the layer above.

nodes.label: 4px Spacing Scale

nodes.label: Semantic Tokens
nodes.rationale: Purpose-based aliases are the only layer that changes on theme switch, so light/dark and rebranding stay one-file edits.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Overrides
nodes.rationale: Only semantic tokens are remapped under .dark, enabling instant theme switching via a single class toggle.

nodes.label: Variant Patterns
nodes.rationale: Variants reassign local --component-* variables instead of rewriting rules, keeping one rule body per component.

nodes.label: HSL CSS Variable Format
nodes.rationale: Storing HSL channels without the function lets Tailwind append opacity modifiers (bg-primary/50) via hsl(var(--primary) / 0.5).

nodes.label: Token Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: --{category}-{item}-{variant}-{state} makes token intent and state readable from the name alone.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Token Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separating raw values, meaning and per-component overrides keeps theme switching and component customization independent.

nodes.label: State Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Never rely on color alone; use aria-disabled/aria-busy/aria-invalid and keep 3:1 minimum contrast for states.

nodes.label: Interactive States
nodes.rationale: State priority (disabled > loading > active > focus > hover > default) resolves conflicts deterministically.

nodes.label: Icon Usage Rules
nodes.rationale: No emoji as structural icons, vector-only assets, token-defined sizes, consistent stroke/fill discipline, and 44pt/48dp touch targets.

nodes.label: Pre-Delivery UI Checklist
nodes.rationale: Visual quality, interaction, light/dark contrast, layout and accessibility checks are verified before delivering UI code, scoped to native app UI.

nodes.label: Rust Async Conventions
nodes.rationale: No blocking calls in async fns (spawn_blocking instead), never hold a std Mutex guard across .await, spawned tasks must be cancellable.

nodes.label: Rust Module Structure
nodes.rationale: Domain modules hold logic with no tauri dependency where possible so they are testable without an app handle.

nodes.label: Tauri Command Rules
nodes.rationale: Commands stay coarse and domain-level (verb_noun, one typed struct for >=3 params) rather than mirroring database CRUD.

nodes.label: Tauri Event Rules
nodes.rationale: Events (domain:event) carry progress and backend-initiated changes, never request/response; long tasks return an id then report by event.

nodes.label: Native Automation Limits
nodes.rationale: tauri-driver does not support iOS or macOS, so native behavior is covered by Rust/Swift unit tests plus manual simulator checks until phase 2.

nodes.label: Test Pyramid
nodes.rationale: Rust unit -> Rust integration -> vitest/Testing Library -> Playwright WebKit E2E -> manual native smoke, each layer scoped to what it can prove.

nodes.label: D2.3 — The offline placeholder decision (implementation of SYNC-4)
nodes.norm_label: d2.3 — the offline placeholder decision (implementation of sync-4)
nodes.rationale: Resolving a photo yields one of four explicit availability states (available locally, fetched now, unavailable offline, missing) decided from the local copy's presence plus a fresh reachability outcome, never from a carried-over status; an entry with unloadable photos must not present as having no photos.

nodes.label: D2.4 — One canonical category catalog per household, established lazily and idempotently
nodes.norm_label: d2.4 — one canonical category catalog per household, established lazily and idempotently
nodes.rationale: The nine canonical categories are held per household (not per device or globally); since P0 created the household record P2 cannot seed the catalog at creation, so it is established lazily on first need and is idempotent on the canonical category so concurrent members converge on exactly one copy.

nodes.label: D2.5 — The dashboard health flag is derived, never stored
nodes.norm_label: d2.5 — the dashboard health flag is derived, never stored
nodes.rationale: Whether a rabbit is flagged is computed on read from its health entries rather than persisted, so the flag stays correct automatically when an entry is edited to lower severity, deleted, or ages out, and no stored state is needed for the threshold-like recomputation.

nodes.label: D2.6 — One interleaved history model
nodes.rationale: Health-only and combined history are one read with different filters, not two pipelines: a single timeline item type ordered by timestamp merges P1 weight entries and P2 health entries and resolves from the already-loaded household collection without a second cold load.

nodes.label: D2.7 — Photo selection is platform-mediated, specifications stay neutral
nodes.norm_label: d2.7 — photo selection is platform-mediated, specifications stay neutral
nodes.rationale: No spec names a picker product; only genuinely platform-divergent behaviour (iOS photo library + permission vs macOS photo source) is tagged, and all permission/scope/entitlement changes are declared by tauri-security while picker bridges belong to apple-native.

nodes.label: D2.8 — Archived rabbits are read-only through one gate
nodes.norm_label: d2.8 — archived rabbits are read-only through one gate
nodes.rationale: All three P2 surfaces that show archived data — health-entry detail, history views and the per-rabbit gallery — consult the single P1 archived gate rather than re-deriving archived-ness, and read access (especially the gallery from an archived rabbit's timeline) stays available.

nodes.label: D2.9 — A displayed photo is kept locally and indefinitely
nodes.norm_label: d2.9 — a displayed photo is kept locally and indefinitely
nodes.rationale: Settles Q1: the local photo copy is not a size-bounded evictable cache but is retained indefinitely until the household or photo is removed, making the SYNC-4 offline guarantee unconditional and the cannot-load placeholder reachable only for a never-displayed photo.

nodes.label: Settled decisions D1–D6
nodes.rationale: D1 connectivity-required saves with no local write queue; D2 owner-dependent sharing (photos count against the owner's storage allowance); D3 no reminders; D4 fresh-start migration (no import path); D5 chart baseline/healthy-range band out; D6 technology-agnostic specs naming no vendor, provider or picker product.

nodes.label: Former open questions Q1–Q3, all settled
nodes.norm_label: former open questions q1–q3, all settled
nodes.rationale: No open questions remain; Q1 (local photo retention) → D2.9, Q2 (profile photo ordering) → D2.10, Q3 (severe-health window) → D2.11, so no task is blocked on an answer.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: A task is done only when every gate command is run fresh and passes, not merely 'should pass'; stated results are required.

nodes.label: Gate Command Sequence
nodes.rationale: Ordered because binding regeneration, formatting and linting must succeed before tests; keeps the same command list as the AGENTS.md table.

nodes.label: iOS Signing and TestFlight Delivery
nodes.rationale: iOS distributes via App Store/TestFlight only, so there is no in-app updater on iOS.

nodes.label: macOS Distribution Decision
nodes.rationale: Mac App Store (same pipeline, sandbox required) vs Developer ID + notarization + updater (no sandbox, own update channel); to be decided by ADR before release work.

nodes.label: Rust Platform Gating
nodes.rationale: cfg(desktop)/cfg(mobile) gates desktop-only plugins; shared code must compile for both aarch64-apple-ios and host macOS, which the gate checks.

nodes.label: Apple Plugin Rules
nodes.rationale: No force-unwrap in Swift, main-thread UI work only, typed errors instead of raw strings, and missing permissions handled as errors not crashes.

nodes.label: Tauri Capabilities
nodes.rationale: One capability file per window/purpose with explicit windows lists and specific permissions preferred over broad defaults.

nodes.label: Content Security Policy
nodes.rationale: default-src 'self' with no unsafe-eval and no remote scripts; CSP is never disabled and inline styles need an ADR.

nodes.label: Per-platform Security Constraints
nodes.rationale: Capabilities carry platforms lists, iOS needs usage-description strings and Keychain secrets, macOS needs minimal sandbox entitlements and hardened runtime.

nodes.label: Tauri Scopes
nodes.rationale: FS limited to app dirs or user-picked paths, shell allowlisted by regex, HTTP allowlisted by origin - least privilege.

nodes.label: Frontend IPC Rules
nodes.rationale: Components never call invoke/bindings directly; AppError.kind is handled explicitly so user messages come from a map.

nodes.label: Rust Error Conventions
nodes.rationale: thiserror in domain code, anyhow only at binary edges, and conversion to AppError at the IPC boundary with a sanitized message.

nodes.label: AppError
nodes.rationale: A tagged thiserror enum (kind/message) lets the frontend switch on kind and avoids leaking paths or secrets in messages.

nodes.label: tauri-specta Typed Bindings
nodes.rationale: src/bindings.ts is generated headlessly via a Rust export and never hand-edited; CI fails on a diff after regeneration to prevent drift.

nodes.label: Mobile-first CSS Rules
nodes.rationale: Base styles are compact and scale up with min-width queries so mobile is the default, never a special case.

nodes.label: Platform Handling
nodes.rationale: src/lib/platform.ts centralizes isMobile/isMacOS/isTouch to avoid scattered user-agent sniffing; UI adapts via adapters, not forked screens.

nodes.label: Adaptive Router Layout
nodes.rationale: One route tree for iOS and macOS; a layout route renders bottom tabs on compact and a sidebar on expanded, and no route relies on native swipe-back.

nodes.label: Hash History Setup
nodes.rationale: Tauri serves static assets, so browser history breaks on reload/deep link; hash history or SPA fallback is required.

nodes.label: Test Viewports
nodes.rationale: Tests run at 390x844 and 1280x800 and must assert adaptive navigation (tabs vs sidebar), not just rendering.

nodes.label: Lifecycle and Connectivity Handling
nodes.rationale: iOS can suspend at any time, so drafts are persisted (never queued writes), reads tolerate offline, and writes are never optimistic.

nodes.label: Frontend State Management Matrix
nodes.rationale: Each kind of state has one designated tool (Query, useState/useReducer, small store, router search params) and no derived state is stored.

nodes.label: Typed Search Params
nodes.rationale: validateSearch with Zod makes the URL the state for filters/tabs/selection that must survive reload.

nodes.label: Design Dials
nodes.rationale: variance/motion/density sliders tune design-system output without changing the query; unset dials leave output unchanged.

nodes.label: ui-ux-pro-max Query Contract
nodes.rationale: Pick the smallest search mode (design-system, one explicit domain, or stack), one dominant intent per query, and verify before persisting results.

nodes.label: Master + Overrides Pattern
nodes.rationale: A project MASTER.md is the global source of truth; page files override it, enabling hierarchical retrieval across sessions without editing Master.
